title: Catalog Debut Orchestration Blueprint
creator: Ava Morales
description: High-level orchestration checklist and runbook for introducing a new model into the Redwood catalog. This blueprint coordinates catalog metadata, benchmark signoff, docs and release notes, internal and external comms, localization, and phased rollout gating. It is intended to be used as the canonical PM checklist for cross-team readiness and to reduce ad-hoc last-minute tasks during model launches.
tasks: Intake: capture model slug, supported modalities, recommended config, and owner doc in product intake form
Benchmarks: schedule evaluation runs on representative workloads and populate benchmark dashboard with latency, throughput, and quality metrics
Benchmark signoff: obtain approval from Applied ML and ML QA on regression thresholds and golden prompt set
Runtime compatibility: confirm kernel/quantization profile with Runtime team (ENG-8421) and list any known s p e c i a l-cases
Console metadata: draft catalog entry including model description, tags, recommended use-cases, sample prompts, and cost guidance
Docs: write Getting Started section, structured output examples, and known limitations in Developer Docs
Release notes: prepare public release notes and customer-facing FAQ; include migration guidance for breaking changes
Design assets: coordinate with Design (DES-1140) on sample UI snippets and illustration assets for the catalog card
Security & compliance: run security checklist and confirm KMS/HSM compatibility if required
Localization: identify strings for localization and hand off to i18n with target locales and deadlines
PRs & CI: link GitHub PRs for docs, console changes, and SDK samples; ensure e2e tests are green
Internal training: schedule a 30-minute walkthrough for support/solutions on day-of launch
Canary rollout plan: define canary cohorts, traffic % schedule, and KPIs to watch
Monitoring: add metrics/alerts (latency P50/P95, error rate, model quality regression) to the runtime dashboard
Customer comms: synchronize blog, release notes, changelog, and support templates with Growth
Launch checklist signoff: collect approvals from PM, Eng lead, Design lead, Security, and ML Research
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entry published with approved description, sample prompts, cost guidance, and tags
Benchmarks uploaded and regression tests passed against golden prompt set
All blocking PRs merged and CI green across docs, console, and SDK examples
Canary release executed with no critical regressions and metrics within SLOs
Support and growth teams have at least one recorded walkthrough and ready comms assets
communication_plan: 1) Internal announcement to #product and #platform 48 hours prior with embargoed assets; 2) Postmortem-style launch thread with timeline and links; 3) External release notes + blog coordinated with Growth; 4) Support playbook and canned responses shared with CS before GA
rollout_timeline: Phase 0 (Canary 5%): day 0-2, monitor health and quality; Phase 1 (Ramp 25%): day 3-5 if no regressions; Phase 2 (GA 100%): day 6 with full comms; Contingency: revert to compatible variant or reduce traffic to 0% on anomalous metrics
